name: Recruit CRM
summary: Applicant tracking system and client CRM for recruitment agencies, with a Chrome sourcing extension, hiring manager portal, AI sourcing and multichannel outreach on a shared credit pool.
best_for: recruitment and staffing agencies that want an applicant tracking system and a client CRM in one place, with a Chrome sourcing extension, a hiring manager portal and, on Business, multichannel outreach and an API
skip_if: you are an in-house HR team hiring for your own company (the product is built around agency clients and placements), you will not use the credit-based features but still pay per seat at agency prices, or you need monthly flexibility with refunds
honest_knock: The headline seat price is not the whole bill: the features recruiters use daily for outreach run on credits, and LinkedIn messaging alone uses 150 credits per user a month while Pro includes 100. The pricing table says unlimited candidates and contacts, but the help centre sets per-user record limits (10,000 each on Pro). Annual billing is charged upfront and the subscription article rules out refunds for unused time, so a wrong tier choice is expensive to undo.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Pro · per user a month billed annually (€95 billed monthly)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-25 on recruitcrm.io/pricing/ with both the Annually and the Monthly toggle clicked, from the Netherlands, where the page shows euros; and in the Recruit CRM help centre) Pro is €79 per user a month billed annually or €95 monthly, with 100 credits per user a month. Business is €109 annually or €135 monthly with 200 credits, and adds the resume formatting agent, multichannel sequences across email, LinkedIn and WhatsApp, white-labelled pages, the open API, SSO, IP whitelisting and 30-day audit logs. Enterprise is €189 annually or €225 monthly with 2,000 credits, Recruit Craft (the career-site builder) included and a named account manager. Credits are pooled across all users in the account and pay for AI sourcing (3 credits per 100 profiles), data enrichment (1 to 4 credits per record), job multiposting (25 credits per job), LinkedIn messaging (150 credits per user a month), WhatsApp (100 per user a month), advanced analytics (300 per user a month) and workflow automation; extra credits can be bought. The help centre says annual billing charges the discounted rate upfront for the whole year. There is a 30-day free trial. Recruit CRM told us it has no discount code for our readers (October 2026). The plan comparison re-read on 1 November 2026 lists the Recruit CRM MCP (for Claude and other AI assistants) as included in Pro, Business and Enterprise, and data migration as a free CSV import tool with assisted migration paid on every plan.

compare_with.name: Top Echelon
compare_with.why: Top Echelon is in our dossiers and lives on Office Software Marketplace: its TE Recruit ATS and CRM was $79 per seat a month billed annually or $95 month to month on Standard when we re-read it on 6 October 2026, and it adds a split-placement network priced per agency. Recruit CRM's Pro is €79 billed annually or €95 monthly (read 25 October 2026, in euros) and leans on AI sourcing, enrichment and multichannel outreach through credits; Top Echelon fits an agency that wants to work split placements with other recruiters.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 2 November 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported two made-up contacts from a CSV file, then exported them again to CSV. We did not open the checkout.
findings: The dashboard showed '30 days left', matching the 30-day trial in the help centre, and the workspace already held sample contacts and candidates.
The importer started every column on 'Don't Import This Column' and had the header row switched off by default, so each field has to be mapped by hand. We found no custom fields in the mapping list.
The import warned that 'all the special characters in FirstName and LastName will be removed', yet both exported first names kept their accents.
The export kept the two contacts with their IDs, but left out the note text we entered: 'Last Note Added' is only a timestamp. The Contact Name column added a trailing space to each name.
Getting the export took four clicks: select the contacts, More, Export, then pick the fields and Export to CSV.

Re-importing the export and how duplicates are matched
